business_scope.primary_industry_name: Real Estate Property Management and Rental Screening Cloud

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Federal jurisdiction; no sub-national fiscal autonomy for corporate law)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Germanic–Swiss school; Swiss Code of Obligations and Civil Code govern corporate and commercial matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–United States Income Tax Treaty (1996, amended by 2009 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Art. 697j et seqq. of the Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) – non-public UBO register of stock companies; Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) of 10 Oct 1997; Ordinance on the Professional Practice of Financial Intermediation (AMLO, SR 955.01); FINMA Circular 2020/01 on AML/CFT; Federal Act on the Enforcement of International Sanctions (Embargo Act, SR 946.231); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Art. 305bis/305ter
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (register maintained internally by the AG; accessible to financial intermediaries, self-regulatory organizations and authorities upon statutory request; not searchable by the public)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of founder's passport (biometric page)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in founder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the country of origin (e.g., Secretary of State in the USA); consular legalization required only for non-Hague parties

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Corporate Existence of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., Delaware Secretary of State, Companies House UK)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-Hague member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or statutory Register of Directors extract of foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate services provider or foreign commercial registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized bank reference letter or proof of funds for the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital of the AG
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank where the founder/subsciber maintains the account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notary-certified copy; used for the professional AML file; apostille not mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn translation into German, French, or Italian of the primary foreign incorporation instruments
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss sworn translator (beeidigter Übersetzer) of the registered canton

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based enhanced due diligence on politically exposed persons under AMLA Art. 3; all UBOs, directors, signatories, and beneficial shareholders screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Swiss SECO sanctions lists under the Embargo Act, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and OFAC SDN list where any US nexus exists; negative media and adverse regulatory news check; five-year record retention per AMLA Art. 7

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex) – official search and registration portal of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register; cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) issues the formal clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be written in Latin script and generally be in one of the four Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh); a name in a foreign language is admissible if pronounceable and not misleading; the statutory suffix for a stock company must be 'Aktiengesellschaft (AG)' or the French/Italian equivalents 'SA' / 'SpA'; the name must satisfy the distinctiveness and truthfulness test under Art. 950 of the Code of Obligations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory pre-reservation exists under Swiss law; the name acquires protection only upon entry in the Commercial Register, but a de facto preliminary clearance is issued by the cantonal registry, and a 30-day window is commonly honored. Upon formal rejection (Verfügung), the founder may file an administrative appeal with the cantonal supervisory authority (e.g., the Directorate of Justice or the Cantonal Administrative Court), within 10 calendar days of receipt; further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court and, ultimately, the Swiss Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht). In practice, re-filing with a corrected distinctive token is faster and more cost-effective.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or fiduciary shared address is generally accepted for a low-risk PropTech/software AG (ISIC 6201) provided it is a real physical address in the registered canton capable of receiving service of process and accessible during normal business hours; actual administrative substance, including a resident director or an authorized Swiss representative with ultimate signatory power, remains mandatory for tax and commercial registry credibility. Pure post-box arrangements without any local substance are rejected by the Commercial Registry and the Federal Tax Administration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 10% to 15% probability of an unannounced registered-office verification within the first 12 months for a standard low-risk SaaS/PropTech AG; the likelihood rises to approximately 25% where the registered office is a shared fiduciary address or the founding shareholder is non-resident. Cantonal Commercial Register Offices and tax authorities may perform physical checks on registered office, corporate records, and signatory availability under the Handelsregisterverordnung.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations), SR 220, Articles 620 to 763 (law of the Aktiengesellschaft / société anonyme), in particular Articles 626 to 632 (formation, share capital and registration) and Article 627 (mandatory articles of association); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, SR 221.411); Federal Act on the Commercial Register (SR 221.411).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), acting under the supervisory framework of the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister / demande d'inscription au registre du commerce) submitted through the eRegister electronic portal, accompanied by the notarially certified Articles of Association (Statuten / statuts) and the bank deposit confirmation required for the paid-up capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Aktiengesellschaft requires a minimum share capital of CHF 100,000, fully subscribed in shares with a minimum par value of CHF 0.01 per share. At least 20% of the nominal value of each share, and in no event less than CHF 50,000 in aggregate, must be paid up prior to registration. The paid-up capital must be deposited in a blocked escrow account opened in the name of the company in formation with a bank or FINMA-licensed financial intermediary in Switzerland. The bank deposit confirmation must accompany the Commercial Register application, and the escrowed funds are released only upon production of the final Commercial Register extract evidencing the registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company with a fully subscribed capital of CHF 100,000 divided into 1,000 registered shares with a par value of CHF 100 each is approved, and the founders' share subscription is ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is adopted at Head Office, 6300 Zug, Canton of Zug, Switzerland, and the Board is authorized to execute the office lease and all deeds incident thereto. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name A] is appointed Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and [Name B] is appointed Member and Chief Financial Officer. All matters requiring board action shall be performed under collective two-signature authority, and the Board of Directors is authorized to open bank accounts, conclude commercial contracts, and file the incorporation with the Commercial Register and the tax authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name clearance and legal feasibility check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zefix Central Business Name Index of the Commercial Register of the Canton of Zug; Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI) Swissreg trademark register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a full-name and free-search query in Zefix to verify the proposed corporate name, confirm the mandatory AG or SA suffix, and check Swissreg for conflicting trademarks or protected names. Verify that the name does not violate Swiss naming principles, is not misleading, and does not infringe third-party rights. Reserve the preferred name through the Commercial Register for the statutory reservation period.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names with two to three alternatives
Draft Articles of Association containing the intended name
Copy of the foundation application or name reservation request
Passports or identity documents of the beneficial owners and directors
Power of attorney for the Swiss-qualified person or formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name conflicts with an existing company or a protected trademark, file an alternative name or obtain a written consent and disclaimer from the rights holder; if the Commercial Register issues conditions, amend the draft Articles of Association and resubmit the clearance request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial deed of formation, adoption of the Articles of Association and appointment of the Board
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public (öffentlich beurkundende Stelle) in the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders appear before a Swiss notary, either in person or through duly authorized representatives, for the authentic execution of the deed of formation. The Articles of Association are read, approved and signed, the share subscription declarations are ratified, and the first Board of Directors is appointed. Each founder must subscribe at least one share. The notary verifies the legality of the formation, the identity of the signatories, and the presence of at least one board member who is resident in Switzerland and authorized to represent the company in accordance with Article 718 of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
required_dossiers: Official passports or identification cards of all founders and board members
Apostilled or consular-certified power of attorney for corporate or offshore founders
Final draft of the Articles of Association with capital structure, share categories and transfer restrictions
Certificate of residence for the Swiss-resident board member
Declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership for the notarial file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect in the draft Articles of Association or insufficient documentation, the documents are corrected and re-executed before the same notary; if a foreign founder's identification or authorization is incomplete, an apostilled certificate is supplied and the deed is signed anew at a supplemental notarial hearing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Swiss bank escrow account and deposit of the minimum paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or financial intermediary licensed by FINMA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked formation account in the name of the company in formation at a Swiss bank or FINMA-licensed financial intermediary. Deposit at least CHF 50,000 representing 20% of the subscribed share capital. The bank performs mandatory KYC and AML verification, issues a written deposit confirmation addressed to the Commercial Register Office, and maintains the account blocked until the company is registered.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed of formation and Articles of Association
Corporate KYC and AML forms signed by the authorized account signatories
Proof of origin of funds for the paid-up capital
Certificate of residence or domicile for each account signatory
Declaration of the ultimate beneficial owner of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional source-of-wealth documentation or rejects an account signatory, supply a sworn statement and bank references, substitute a different authorized signatory, or transfer the escrow to another Swiss bank or FINMA-licensed institution; reissue of the deposit confirmation is obtained from the accepting institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the registration application with the Commercial Register of the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration through the eRegister portal or in hard copy at the Commercial Register Office. The application is accompanied by the notarially certified Articles of Association, the bank deposit confirmation, the list of board members, and the signed declarations of the board regarding compliance with Swiss law. The Commercial Register verifies the legality of the formation and, upon approval, enters the company in the register, thereby conferring legal personality.
required_dossiers: Signed and dated Commercial Register application form (Anmeldung)
Notarially certified Articles of Association
Bank deposit confirmation evidencing payment of at least CHF 50,000
List of board members stating names, citizenship, residence and signature authority
Duly executed specimen signatures of all authorized signatories
Declaration of the board confirming compliance with the Swiss-resident representation requirement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register raises an objection, respond in writing within the statutory abatement period of 30 days and amend the deficient documents; if the application is rejected, cure the defects and resubmit, or file an appeal with the Cantonal Administrative Court of Zug (Verwaltungsgericht des Kantons Zug) within 30 days of the decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SHAB publication, UID allocation and issuance of the Commercial Register extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB / Feuille officielle suisse du commerce); Federal Statistical Office for the UID register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of registration, the Commercial Register transmits the incorporation data for publication in the SHAB. The company is automatically assigned a unique Swiss business identification number (UID / Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer). Obtain the certified Commercial Register extract evidencing the legal existence, capital and registered office of the company; the extract is the official proof of incorporation required for banking, tax and contractual purposes.
required_dossiers: Registration confirmation issued by the Commercial Register
Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
Reference to the SHAB publication notice or official gazette excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication is delayed or contains erroneous data, request a correction order from the Commercial Register Office and ensure a corrected notice is re-published; if the UID is not received automatically, apply to the Federal Statistical Office through the UID portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation tax, social insurance and municipal registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) for VAT; Cantonal Tax Office of Zug (Finanzdirektion des Kantons Zug); Zug Compensation Office (AHV/IV/EO); Cantonal Labor Inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the Zug Compensation Office for AHV/IV/EO social insurance contributions within 30 days of incorporation; open the employer payroll account; register with the Cantonal Tax Office for corporate income tax; complete VAT registration if taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 100,000 per business year or if foreign B2B services are rendered; verify mandatory accident insurance coverage with SUVA or a private insurer; notify the municipal office of the physical workplace for occupational health and safety supervision where applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register extract and UID confirmation
Copy of the registered office lease or tenancy agreement
Payroll estimates and list of employees or directors
Passports and residence permits of all employees and directors
Completed VAT registration application and corporate tax registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compensation office or tax administration requires supplementary information, provide the requested documents within the set deadline; if late registration is identified, a written justification and retroactive registration are submitted to avoid penalty assessments; any objection to the VAT or tax registration decision may be appealed to the competent cantonal or federal tax authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Department of Economics and Labour of the Canton of Zug (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit des Kantons Zug) for business operations; Gebäudeversicherung Zug for fire safety clearances; Cantonal Labor Inspectorate for workplace safety oversight.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial or manufacturing operating license is required for the software, property technology and SaaS platform activities under ISIC 6201. The company operates under its Commercial Register entry, the ordinary municipal business registration, and the occupational safety and fire protection clearances required for the office workspace.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt), delegated to the Office for the Environment of the Canton of Zug (Amt für Umweltschutz des Kantons Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a formal environmental impact assessment. The activity of software development and cloud-based property management does not fall within the list of installations requiring an EIA under Annex 1 to the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfungs-Verordnung, SR 814.011).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Operations are limited to office and IT activities; no industrial wastewater or VOC process emissions are generated. Sanitary discharges must comply with municipal sewage regulations of the City of Zug. Electronic and electrical waste, including end-of-life IT equipment, must be returned through the systems of the Swiss Ordinance on the Return, Take-back and Disposal of Electrical and Electronic Equipment (ORDEE). No on-site data centers are operated, so no specific coolant or energy consumption thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The office premises require a basic fire safety confirmation under the guidelines of the Swiss Fire Protection Association (VKF), including compliance with escape route, fire extinguisher and smoke alarm requirements, verified by Gebräudeversicherung Zug or the municipal fire prevention authority. Structural load inspections apply only to the standard office occupancy limits and do not require a special engineering clearance. Occupational health and safety measures must comply with the Swiss Labor Act (Arbeitsgesetz) and the Swiss Accident Prevention Ordinance (VUV), including ergonomic workplace design, accident prevention training, and mandatory accident insurance through SUVA or a private insurer under the Swiss Federal Act on Accident Insurance (UVG).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions – AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni – AFC); official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; VAT registration and returns are processed via the ESTV 'Sage' e-services platform and the Swiss Federal Tax Administration VAT portal at https://www.estv.admin.ch/estv/en/home/value-added-tax.html.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG): (1) Establish the entity in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister), which generates the permanent eleven-digit Swiss Business Identification Number (UID – Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer). (2) Register for VAT with the ESTV using Form 130 (Anmeldung zur Mehrwertsteuerpflicht) within 30 days after exceeding the statutory threshold or upon commencement of taxable activities in Switzerland; the ESTV issues a separate MWST-registration number (VAT ID) in the format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX MWST. (3) For a foreign non-established supplier, registration is mandatory where Swiss taxable turnover (excluding VAT) exceeds CHF 100,000, or immediately in the case of supplies of electronically supplied digital services (SaaS) to non-business consumers (B2C) within Switzerland (Art. 10, para. 3 MTWSTG). (4) Files periodic VAT returns (quarterly, semi-annual or annual based on turnover) through the ESTV 'Sage' portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. Material statutory elections available to a Swiss AG with international scope: (a) VAT group taxation election per Art. 12 MWSTG for closely aligned domestic entities; (b) cantonal patent/IP box election for qualifying IP profits at reduced cantonal rates; (c) participation relief election (statutory) for capital gains and dividends from qualifying participations of ≥ 10% or CHF 1 million market value; (d) notional interest deduction (NID) election for Swiss finance branches or financing companies in designated cantons; (e) restructuring step-up and deemed-liquidation election. Switzerland implements OECD BEPS hybrid mismatch rules via the Swiss Hybrid Mismatch Ordinance (HSR) effective 1 January 2020, denying deduction for hybrid mismatch arrangements even absent a domestic 'check-the-box' mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual global taxable turnover excluding VAT and exempt supplies (Art. 10 Swiss VAT Act – MWSTG). For non-established suppliers of electronic services (B2C), registration is required when the annual turnover from Swiss private consumers exceeds CHF 100,000; B2B supplies to Swiss VAT-registered businesses transfer the VAT liability to the recipient under the reverse-charge rule, which does not trigger the supplier's registration obligation except where physical nexus or e-services thresholds apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate is currently imposed by the ESTV. Swiss invoices must satisfy minimum statutory content under Art. 26 MWSTG (supplier name and address, MWST-ID/UID, date, description, rate, and tax amount). Since 30 June 2020, QR-billing (Swiss QR Code / QR-Rechnung) is mandatory as the standard payable channel for all Swiss business invoices referencing a Swiss IBAN. E-invoicing (Peppol BIS / eBill) is available on a voluntary basis; there is no mandatory API integrated clearance. VAT returns are filed electronically via the ESTV 'Sage' e-services portal at regulated intervals, generally quarterly for taxable turnover exceeding CHF 5,005,000 (2024), otherwise semi-annual or annual.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical goods: zero-rated at 0% under Art. 23(1) MWSTG if the goods are permanently exported outside Switzerland by the supplier or a third party and the export is substantiated via a customs declaration from the Swiss customs authority. Cross-border services (SaaS/PaaS licence subscriptions, cloud-based real-estate screening, property-management software): strictly zero-rated / out of scope of Swiss VAT where the place of supply (Art. 8 MWSTG and Arts. 17-18 VAT Ordinance – MWSTV) is deemed abroad, i.e., the B2B recipient is established in a foreign country and receives the e-service in that foreign establishment; for B2C, the recipient's habitual residence abroad. Claim requires documented evidence of the recipient's foreign establishment (copy of foreign VAT registration, business registry extract) and the service contract stating the place of supply; the supply must be reported in the VAT return as an export with input tax deduction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For physical goods export: Swiss customs export declaration (A.Be.080, lodged electronically via e-dec/Import and Export System), Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note, and commercial invoice evidencing foreign destination.

For SaaS cross-border services: executed supply contract / statement of work with the foreign business customer, itemised VAT invoice (or reverse-charge statement), official foreign VAT registration certificate or business registry excerpt of the recipient proving foreign establishment, and Swiss bank account statements / SWIFT MT103 showing receipt of the foreign remittance in settlement of the exported service.

Inward remittance / FX repatriation substantiation: Swiss bank account statement evidencing credit of foreign currency proceeds and, if converted, the conversion entry; no formal 'Inward Remittance Certificate' exists under Swiss practice but the bank statement & SWIFT MT103 serve as the de facto instrument.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV may review export zero-rating for up to 10 years of backlog (Art. 42 MWSTG) and will claw back input VAT, impose charging tax, and require retrospective reassessment where the foreign-supply criteria are not substantiated or where the arrangement is found to be a sham. Penalties are governed by Arts. 70-73 MWSTG: (i) procedural violations: fines up to CHF 20,000; (ii) attempted tax evasion: fine up to 1x the tax evaded; (iii) completed tax evasion: fine up to 3x the tax evaded, plus default interest at the statutory rate of 4.5% p.a.; (iv) fraudulent evasion or forgery of export documentation triggers criminal sanctions under the Customs Surveillance and Security Act (CSSA), including custodial sentences and substantial fines. Where the entity fails to repatriate foreign exchange or presents false inward remittance documentation, the zero-rated treatment is retrospectively annulled, the VAT is recharged at the standard 8.1% rate, and input tax credits on associated cost bases are denied.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains a fully convertible currency regime for both current and capital account transactions. The Swiss franc (CHF) is freely traded on global FX markets, and there are no Swiss exchange control laws or regulations restricting the conversion of CHF into foreign currency, nor any restrictions on the repatriation of capital, dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees to non-residents. Cross-border capital movements are subject to standard financial market regulations, anti-money laundering laws, and prudential banking requirements, but not to licensing or prior approval by the SNB. Profit remittances from a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) are generally unrestricted; however, dividend distributions are subject to Swiss withholding tax at 35%, a portion of which may be reclaimed under an applicable double taxation treaty, and the company must ensure corporate law solvency and documentation requirements are satisfied. There is no differentiation between capital and current account convertibility as a matter of Swiss federal law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation. There are no mandatory timelines for the repatriation of export-related foreign currency receivables, no conversion ratios, and no requirement to channel export proceeds through a particular Swiss bank. Swiss-resident exporters may hold foreign currency accounts offshore or domestically at their discretion, and may use such proceeds for operational liquidity, reinvestment, or FX hedging in accordance with normal treasury policies. The only relevant obligations arise under anti-money laundering due-diligence rules and, if applicable, the Swiss Federal Act on the Free Movement of Capital, which itself contains no surrender or conversion mandates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CHF / EUR / USD multi-currency current account)
Operational Account and dedicated Escrow / Client Funds Account (for property rental security deposits)
Operational Account with integrated treasury and online banking platform

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium — strictly limited to non-deposit-taking payment service arrangements. Swiss law does not grant a passport or automatic mutual recognition to fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) licensed in the EU/EEA or in other jurisdictions. An offshore EMI that performs deposit-taking or public-refinancing activities in Switzerland requires a FINMA banking or Fintech license under the Swiss Financial Institutions Act (FinIA). However, pure payment transaction processing, without deposit taking in Switzerland, may be provided by a non-Swiss PSP on a cross-border basis, subject to compliance with Swiss AML/CFT legislation, data protection rules, and client disclosure duties. For a PropTech SaaS platform handling rental payments, custody of client funds in an EMI account may be constructed as a contractual sub-accounting arrangement rather than a Swiss bank account, but this raises legal recharacterization risk if the platform becomes a de facto deposit taker. Therefore, the viability of offshore EMIs is best used for payment initiation and settlement facilitation, not for holding client funds earmarked as rental deposits, which should be entrusted to a Swiss-licensed bank or a FINMA-authorized fintech.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a typical Swiss Aktiengesellschaft with non-resident shareholders, most leading Swiss banks require the ultimate beneficial owner, the signatories, and, in practice, at least one member of the board of directors to appear in person for a face-to-face KYC interview. Strictly remote account opening is generally limited to small, low-risk Swiss-resident sole proprietorships; for an AG with offshore shareholders and an active cross-border SaaS business, a physical meeting at the bank's premises in Switzerland, or at an approved Swiss embassy or notary office, is normally mandatory. Some banks provide a hybrid onboarding path combining digital documentary upload and a video call, but they condition final acceptance on production of original notarised documents and, in many cases, a subsequent physical visit by compliance officers. For the statutory duty to open accounts under Swiss anti-money laundering rules, the bank must obtain reliable information on the beneficial owner; failure to meet the interview requirement is the most common reason for rejection or prolonged escalation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore beneficial owners without a clear economic rationale or substance in Switzerland
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provided dossier should include: (i) registered articles of association and commercial register extract of the Swiss AG; (ii) detailed organisational charts showing ultimate individuals and intermediate holding structures; (iii) substantiated business plan proving genuine SaaS operations and commercial tenants; (iv) board resolutions approving the bank relationship and specifying treasury signing authorities; (v) professional references from home-jurisdiction legal counsel and auditors; (vi) notarised and apostilled passports and proof of address; and (vii) a written explanation of why the Swiss entity controls and invoices the Group's international property management clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction volume of payment collections from residential real estate tenants lacking transparent rental contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File a master omnibus compliance pack containing: (i) a complete register of tenants and landlords with screening against Swiss and international sanctions lists; (ii) copies of representative property management agreements and rental agreements proving the platform's agency or SaaS-collection role; (iii) an AML/CFT policy manual with risk-based transaction monitoring thresholds; (iv) records of dual-control workflows and segregation of client funds from operational funds; and (v) periodic transaction reports with audit trail showing the automatic allocation of funds to the correct landlord or escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of modern e-money or 'pass-through' accounts for escrowing tenant security deposits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a legal opinion from Swiss counsel confirming that the platform does not engage in unauthorised deposit-taking. The dossier must include: (i) the signed escrow agreement naming a Swiss licensed bank as custodian; (ii) platform terms and conditions for tenants showing clear disclosure that deposits remain owned by tenants and are held in segregated bank accounts; (iii) audited financial statements of the Swiss AG; (iv) a FINMA-compliant AML-organisation regulation with a named money-laundering reporting officer; (v) documented evidence of outsourcing due diligence to FINMA-regulated intermediaries if applicable; and (vi) a description of the technical clearing architecture whereby settlement is pushed to the landlord's bank account only after payment finality is confirmed by the PSP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Automated, recurring payment flows without purpose codes or invoice references, triggering suspicions of hidden fees or money movement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Implementation of a clean data package demonstrating commercial substance: (i) machine-readable invoices and receipts linked to unique payment reference IDs; (ii) an anti-fraud reconciliation ledger showing each payment stream mapped to a specific property and landlord; (iii) standardised SWIFT or SEPA XML messages with transparent remittance information; (iv) customer records showing business relationships with registered property owners; and (v) an externally reviewed audit trail proving that all collections exceeding CHF 15,000 are batch-reviewed by a compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions into a Swiss AG from non-resident shareholders are freely permitted and require no exchange-control approval or special licence. The compliant routing protocol is to effect the injection by means of a SWIFT wire transfer in CHF, EUR, or USD from the shareholder's account to the Swiss operating account, with clear payment narrative quoting the company's purpose, e.g., 'CHF Share Capital Increase under Art. 652 of the Swiss Code of Obligations' or 'Paid-in capital — par value and premium'. The Swiss bank debiting the account will require the uploading of a certified board resolution approving the capital increase, minutes of the extraordinary general meeting, and, if the subscription is in currency other than CHF, a currency conversion statement from the company's auditor. The bank will obtain a statement of compliance with Swiss anti-money laundering rules; the payer may require a beneficiary reference / IRB (International Bank Reference Number) for internal reporting. In practice, the wire should be directed through the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system or euroSIC for EUR, and, if the amount exceeds CHF 15,000, the bank's AML transaction monitoring system will automatically record the reason for payment; the company should be ready to furnish the share register and a notarised declaration from the beneficial owner confirming the source of funds from legitimate business or personal wealth.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border trade and SaaS service disbursements from Switzerland, the principal clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for direct straight-through payments, TARGET2/euroSIC for EUR disbursements, and SIC for CHF. For larger or more structured property-remediation and construction settlements under which a PropTech platform manages supplier payments, a Documentary Letter of Credit (LC) may be issued by a Swiss bank on behalf of the AG, with the supplier's bank as advising bank; however, given the recurring, low-margin nature of SaaS subscription fees, MT103 transfers are the default, with a robust audit trail of invoice numbers and purpose codes. For outbound payments to partners in non-SWIFT jurisdictions, priority should be given to SWIFT-compliant correspondent banking chains with a Swiss clearing bank, ensuring that the remitting bank executes the payment in compliance with Swiss Federal Office of Police economic sanctions and maintains the full remitter mandate under the FATF Recommendation 16. Payout settlements to international landlords can also be batched via SWIFT netting, but each beneficiary identity and tax-reference field must be maintained in the treasury workbench to avoid suspicious-transaction filings.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Book-entry spot FX contracts for immediate conversions between CHF, EUR, and USD, executed through a Swiss-licensed bank or a regulated FX prime broker.
FX forward contracts on physically deliverable CHF/EUR and CHF/USD cross rates, with a maximum maturity up to five years for a corporate non-financial counterparty under standard ISDA documentation.
FX swaps combining an FX spot transaction with a forward transaction for periodic treasury rebalancing of the platform's EUR-technology-procurement and CHF-revenue streams.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for hedging any long-term CHF or Euro debt exposure, permitted with a Swiss bank or international swap dealer, provided that the AG qualifies as a financial counterparty or takes the small non-financial counterparty threshold only if transaction notional is modest.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for hedging residual exposure to illiquid or developing-market currencies such as RMB, INR, BRL, or TRY, permitted as off-book derivatives via a FINMA-regulated dealer, allowing net settlement in CHF while circumventing local currency convertibility restrictions in the counterparty's jurisdiction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return (combined federal, cantonal and municipal corporate tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration as administering body, together with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for federal tax matters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: due within 3 to 4 months after balance-sheet date; for a standard 31 December fiscal year, the cantonal deadline is commonly between 31 March and 30 June, with extension to 30 September available on request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers default assessment, late interest and procedural fines typically between CHF 100 and CHF 1,000; deliberate understatement may lead to criminal tax evasion fines and, for sustained non-payment, bankruptcy and commercial-register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value added tax (VAT) return by the taxable AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly returns are due within 60 days after the close of each calendar quarter; entities assigned annual VAT reporting must file no later than 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest applies to unpaid VAT; deliberate or grossly negligent omission exposes the company to penalties of up to 30% of the tax evaded. Persistent non-filing may result in blockage of the VAT number and administrative seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage and contribution statement for state social insurance (AHV/AVS, IV, EO, ALV, BVG/LPP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Employer's Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse); occupational pension data reported to the registered BVG/LPP pension institution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual employer wage data must be submitted by 31 January following the calendar year; quarterly contribution payments are payable at quarter end within statutory terms.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid employee contribution deductions create arrears with default interest; administrative fines for reporting violations may reach CHF 10,000, and withholding employee social contributions can constitute a criminal offence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Adoption of annual financial statements by the shareholders' meeting and signing of accounts by the board of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (submission copy); no general filing with the Commercial Register unless an auditor or capital measure requires publication; records retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: the ordinary shareholders' meeting must be held within six months after the balance-sheet date under Art. 699 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; for a 31 December year-end, the meeting is normally held by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM within the statutory deadline is an act of non-compliance by the board; a court may order the meeting at the company's cost and directors may face liability for resulting losses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner confirmation and share-register verification annex included with the annual tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority for the declaration annex and Swiss Federal Reporting Office for Legal Entities (Zentrales Register der wirtschaftlichen Eigentümer) in trigger situations involving bearer shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual submission with the corporate tax return; share transfers or beneficial-owner changes are recorded in the share register promptly, and central-report triggers are filed within 30 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or false beneficial-ownership declarations attract tax and regulatory penalties; bearer-share reporting violations may subject the company to fines up to CHF 500,000 and responsible officers to fines up to CHF 50,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full statutory audit is compulsory when the AG exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: balance-sheet total CHF 20 million (approx. US$22 million), turnover CHF 40 million (approx. US$44 million), and 250 annual FTE employees. If these are not exceeded, a limited statutory examination (review) is required when two of three lower thresholds are exceeded for two years: CHF 1 million assets, CHF 2 million turnover, and 10 FTE employees. Below those limits, shareholders may unanimous opt out of audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations Arts. 957-963b; Swiss GAAP FER is the prevailing financial-reporting framework; IFRS is mandatory for listed groups and permitted for other AGs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not impose a separate federal annual UBO form; the annual corporate tax return contains a shareholder and beneficial-owner declaration, and the board must confirm the correctness of the share register at each annual meeting. Registered-share transfers require timely updating of the Aktienregister; bearer-share AGs must notify the Swiss Federal Reporting Office for Legal Entities of beneficial-owner changes within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 1,100-4,300 per year (CHF 1,000-3,900) for registered-office use, agent and corporate-housekeeping services from a Swiss fiduciary provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 7,500-25,000 for a limited statutory examination; US$ 35,000-100,000 for a full ordinary audit, depending on complexity, group structure and consolidation requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal statutory corporate income tax on net profit (the federal effective rate is approximately 7.83% because the federal tax itself is deductible; in the unitary model used in this dossier cantonal/communal taxes are not distinguished).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for standard AG; available incentives include the federal R&D super deduction (additional deduction of 10% up to max 30% of federal wage base for qualifying R&D in most cantons) and the patent box regime allowing a 90% exemption of qualifying IP net royalty income; participation exemption applies for dividends and capital gains on qualifying holdings of at least 10%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss composite corporate tax return for legal entities (cantonal form 'Tax Return for Legal Entities' with integrated federal direct tax assessment); e-filing is available through the cantonal tax authority's electronic portal (e.g., ForMax, win-tax).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 6 months after the end of the business year (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); extension of up to an additional 6 months is available on written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: AG legal name, Swiss registered office and address, UID/VAT number, fiscal year-end, purpose, and participation holdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Swiss AG with non-resident directors or shareholders, provide exact contact details of the registered office and the Swiss tax representative; all statutory records must remain at the registered seat in Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory balance sheet under Swiss Code of Obligations (minimum chart of accounts), including share capital, statutory capital reserve, retained earnings, provisions, and asset and liability detail.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All intercompany receivables/payables must be evidenced by written agreements and arm's-length interest terms; unrecognised income from non-resident related parties must be disclosed in the annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss itemisation: gross revenue, direct costs, operating expenses, depreciation, financial result, extraordinary items and net profit before taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SaaS subscriptions from the PropTech platform are recognised on a straight-line basis per Swiss GAAP FER; transaction costs (Stripe, ACH) are deductible; any cross-border licence or management fees to group entities must be justified on a functional and risk analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recalculation of taxable profit: add-back of non-deductible expenses (hidden profit distributions, excessive interest, artistic or representation costs not commercially justified) and deduction of tax-free income (capital gains, participation dividends, IP-box income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to shareholders or related parties in excess of what would be at arm's length result in deemed distributions subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax; the AG must self-report these adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule for deduction of dividend income from qualifying participations (≥10%) and income from qualifying patents and similar rights applying the patent box formula.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the exact ownership period and percentage; for non-resident shareholders, this section does not affect personal WHT, but the AG must maintain documentary evidence of the IP developed in Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal and cantonal withholding taxes withheld on the AG's own income (e.g., dividends, interest), foreign tax credits, and instalment prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign WHT on cross-border SaaS revenue can be credited against Swiss corporate tax if a DTA applies; the AG must provide official certificates of taxes paid abroad.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a warning, then a 'Säumnisentschädigung' (default surcharge) of up to 0.5% per month of the assessed federal tax, capped at 20%; procedural fines up to CHF 10,000 for deliberate failure (canton plus federal). Repeated non-filing leads to an estimated assessment and can be treated as tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividend distributions of a Swiss AG.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A foreign corporate shareholder may apply for full or partial refund of the 35% WHT under the applicable DTA by submitting a refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (SFTA) within three years of the dividend payment, attaching a valid country-of-residence certificate (TRC) and proof of beneficial ownership. Where the DTA rate is 0% (e.g., 10%+ participation in certain treaties), the refund is complete; for portfolio holdings a 15% treaty rate is common. The refund is processed via SFTA directly; a relief at source mechanism is not available for ordinary dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: No Swiss WHT on royalties - licence fees paid by a Swiss AG to a non-resident are not subject to Swiss withholding tax, although the licensee may claim the expense and the recipient is taxed in its residence country. Interest on ordinary intercompany loans is also free of Swiss WHT; however, interest on Swiss-issued bonds ('obligations') is subject to 35% WHT. Treaty rates for interest vary between 0% and 10% (most Swiss DTAs provide for 0-5% for banks and 5-10% for others), and royalties are generally exempt from Swiss source WHT under Swiss treaty practice.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 900,000,000 group consolidated annual revenue (mandatory Master File and Local File for direct federal tax purposes; CbC report required for ultimate parent groups meeting the threshold). Below this threshold, the AG is expected to keep contemporaneous arm's-length documentation for any material related-party transaction when requested by the Swiss tax authority, particularly for SaaS platform licensing, software development, and management fees.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland applies a substance-over-form doctrine under Art. 57 of the Federal Direct Tax Act and Art. 10 of the Withholding Tax Act. There is no separate Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) framework as in the UAE; however, treaty benefits, participation exemption and IP tax incentives are denied if the AG does not have sufficient economic substance in Switzerland (adequate office space, local employees, actual management decisions, and core business activities). A PropTech SaaS AG must ensure that its cloud platform development, customer contracts, and product management decisions are demonstrably executed in Switzerland.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful or grossly negligent omission of revenue or overstatement of deductions in the tax return, falsification of books and records, or concealment of the true consideration received from the PropTech SaaS subscriptions or client screening payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to 100% of the evaded federal tax plus the tax due and interest; cantonal penal surcharges up to CHF 20,000; the claim for tax also survives a liquidation of the AG. In severe cases, criminal prosecution leads to imprisonment of the responsible person.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency of the AG if they personally participated in or negligently failed to stop the evasion. This can lead to civil restitution of the tax stolen, a travel ban (12 months or more), and imprisonment up to 1 year for wilful evasion (Art. 175 DBG).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-filing / Late Filing of Annual Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the annual corporate tax return within the statutory deadline (6 months after year-end) without extension, despite formal written reminder from the cantonal tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Procedural fine up to CHF 10,000; automatic assessment for 3 years at the tax administration's discretion (Ermessenveranlagung); a default surcharge equal to 0.5% per month of the assessed federal tax, capped at 20%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who is personally responsible for the filing and who fails after warning is subject to a personal fine of up to CHF 2,000; for persistent refusal, imprisonment for up to 6 months (Art. 196 DBG).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Swiss AG as a letterbox conduit to channel royalties, dividends, or platform income from a non-resident parent to tax optimisation without real Swiss management and development activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and statutory exemptions (participation, IP box); recharacterisation of income as taxable profit; recomputation of withholding tax on deemed distributions; fines up to 100% of the tax benefit (Art. 57 DBG / Art. 10 VStG).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintain the shell status are jointly and severally liable for all underpaid taxes, and may face criminal sanction for false certification; if they sign annual substance declarations they also incur civil liability under Art. 754 CO.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PropTech platform as a payment-collection intermediary for rental payments and tenant screening without implementing the required KYC and AML controls under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act, especially where payments are settled via ACH or Stripe across borders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to CHF 500,000; cancellation of a required polygraph licence if the activity requires one; in extreme cases dissolution of the company and confiscation of assets (Art. 41 GwG).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the authorised money-laundering compliance officer face personal criminal liability with imprisonment up to 3 years and fines (Art. 305bis Criminal Code); the corporate veil is pierced for recovery of assets from unlawful activity.
